Global caveats

Issue Reading note
Fiscal 2026 is unreported and prints in three days Every FY2026 figure here is nine reported months plus guidance, or a consensus estimate for a year that has already elapsed. Three conclusions resolve in that print: whether the 40% Q3 next-generation firewall bookings growth converted to revenue, whether the guided 28.9-29.2% full-year non-GAAP operating margin was reached (which needs 28.5-29.6% in Q4 against 27.1% in Q3), and what a first full quarter of CyberArk does to the margin.
The reported line and the organic line diverge by 17 points Chronosphere consolidated from 2026-01-29 and CyberArk from 2026-02-11. In the April 2026 quarter they contributed $388m of revenue and a $523m operating loss. Reported revenue grew 31.1%, organic 14.2%; NGS ARR grew 60% reported and 28% organic; RPO 36% and 22%. Management gave that split twice and said on 2026-06-02 it will stop giving it.
There is no GAAP revenue by platform PANW discloses revenue only by geographic theatre and by product / subscription / support. Management said it intends to report Network Security, Cortex and Identity revenue from fiscal 2027. Every platform split in this document is management commentary from a call or an estimate whose arithmetic is shown.
GAAP and non-GAAP diverge by more than twenty points of margin FY2025 GAAP operating margin was 13.5% against a 28.8% non-GAAP margin, and most of the gap is $1,295m of share-based compensation. In the April 2026 quarter the GAAP operating margin was −6.1% and the non-GAAP margin 27.1%. The two bases are never mixed in one comparison here.

The CyberArk price appears in two forms and they are not interchangeable: $25bn of equity value at the 2025-07-30 announcement, and $21,061m of purchase consideration booked at the 2026-02-11 close. The difference is a 16.1% decline in PANW's own share price between those dates plus $680m of replacement awards charged to post-close service.

1. Business description, model and unit economics

Palo Alto Networks sells enterprise security in three commercial forms, all of them subscriptions attached to something already deployed.▪ It sells firewalls in four form factors that run one operating system, and eleven cloud-delivered subscriptions plus premium support against the roughly one million appliances already in customers' racks. It sells a security-operations platform that replaces a legacy SIEM and the analyst hours around it, a cloud-security platform, and an observability platform bought in January 2026. Since 11 February 2026 it also sells identity security, the CyberArk business rebranded Idira. Substantially all revenue moves through a two-tier channel: PANW bills distributors, distributors bill resellers, resellers bill end customers in over 180 countries, including almost all of the Fortune 100 (FY2025 10-K, Item 1).

What drives the economics

Price. PANW does not publish its prices. A European authorised reseller publishes net list prices per SKU, and the ratios are near-identical across a 22x span of appliance price: each advanced subscription lists at about 27% of the appliance price a year and premium support at about 19% (enbitcon.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web]. The appliance is therefore a price index for everything attached to it, and a throughput upgrade lifts the subscription annuity proportionally without a separate negotiation. At the disclosed attach of more than four subscriptions per installed device, the annual recurring bill at list is 4 × 27% + 19% = 127% of the box price, so across a five-year deployment the customer pays roughly 6.4x the appliance price in subscriptions and support and the box is about 14% of five-year spend.▪ Realised price also moves: PANW raised hardware list prices in September and November 2021, on 2022-08-01, on 2023-08-01, and by 10% in early April 2026 (Q3 FY2026 call).

Outside Network Security the pricing base changes. XSIAM's average contract value is anchored near $1m because that is roughly what a mid-size enterprise SIEM licence plus its analyst overhead costs; Arora's framing is "you come and say, 'I know you're spending $10 million a year running your SOC. I can do it for $9 million'" (Q1 FY2025 call). Chronosphere is sold at "approximately half the cost of what the industry charges" (Q3 FY2026 call), described two quarters earlier as "$0.40 of dollar of competitive options" (UBS conference, 2025-12-02). Identity is licensed three ways, per user for the workforce and developer products, per target system for endpoint privilege management, and per machine and credential for machine identity (CYBR 20-F FY2024, Item 5).

Volume. The count of enforcement points deployed, the count of legacy SIEM contracts reaching renewal, and the count of privileged accounts inside roughly 10,000 enterprises. The driver tree below decomposes each.

Cost. Not silicon. Non-cancelable purchase commitments at 2026-04-30 were $8,092m for cloud hosting against $246m for manufacturing, and the whole manufacturing commitment falls inside FY2027 (Q3 FY2026 10-Q, Note 11).▪ Cloud hosting service costs rose $189.5m in FY2025 and $171m across nine months of FY2026, of which $75m landed in the April quarter alone. Marginal cloud hosting cost per incremental dollar of NGS ARR went from 9.1% in FY2024 to 14.0% in FY2025 to 18.6% across nine months of FY2026.▪

Building the reported product gross margin from the appliance and software rows gives 0.58 × 62% + 0.42 × 95% = 75.9% against 77.1% reported, a 1.2-point gap. The same build for FY2021, when hardware was 76% of product revenue and product gross margin 72.5%, implies a hardware gross margin near 66%, so the appliance line declined two to four points across four years while the blended product margin rose.

One reconciliation does not close, and it bears on the largest revenue line in the company. Support revenue of $2,445.2m in FY2025 against roughly one million installed appliances is about $2,400 per device a year, nearly three times the 19% list ratio. Either most support revenue attaches to software licences, SASE and subscriptions, or the supported base is larger than the one-million figure. PANW does not decompose support revenue, so the per-device series is a blended annuity across everything attached to an appliance.

2. Key technologies and technical differentiators

One technical asset is hard to copy, and it is a deployment position: about one million firewalls in the field, 125 million sensors and 17 petabytes of daily telemetry, all of it inline in customer traffic (Q3 FY2026 call).▪ Every detection product PANW sells is trained and enforced from that position. The rest of the portfolio — eleven cloud-delivered subscriptions, the SASE products, the CNAPP, the observability platform, the identity platform — has been bought or matched by a named competitor within two to three years.

PAN-OS and the single-pass architecture. PAN-OS is one operating system across appliance, VM-Series virtual, CN-Series container and Cloud NGFW as a managed service. A policy written once applies everywhere, and a customer moving a workload from a data centre to a VPC does not rewrite it. The FY2016 10-K described the underlying design as SP3, "our proprietary software and hardware architecture… comprised of two elements: single-pass software and parallel processing hardware": the packet is parsed once and every enabled inspection runs against that parse, instead of chaining engines that each re-parse. Current hardware uses PANW-designed silicon, with the PA-7500 specified at up to 1.5 Tbps of App-ID throughput on the FE400 ASIC (paloaltonetworks.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web].

The company's own disclosure records what changed. App-ID, User-ID, Content-ID, SP3 and "single-pass" appear 33 times in the FY2016 10-K and 34 times in each of FY2017 through FY2019; 7 times in FY2020 and FY2021; 3 times in FY2023 and FY2024; and not at all in the FY2025 10-K. What the FY2025 10-K puts in their place is a distribution property: PAN-OS gives "a consistent set of capabilities across our entire network security product line," identically from the PA-400 to the PA-7500 and in VM-Series, CN-Series and Cloud NGFW. That advantage is real and it is the one that pays, because it converts a hardware refresh into a subscription annuity. It is delivered through software packaging, and no physics or ecosystem barrier protects it.▪ Fortinet ships the FortiGate 7121F at up to 1.2 Tbps on its own NP7 and CP9 ASICs, and Gartner's inaugural 2025 Hybrid Mesh Firewall Magic Quadrant named Palo Alto Networks, Fortinet, Check Point and Juniper as Leaders together (sdxcentral.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web].

Cloud-delivered security services. Eleven advanced subscriptions ride the installed firewall base: Advanced Threat Prevention, Advanced WildFire, Advanced URL Filtering, Advanced DNS Security, IoT/OT Device Security, GlobalProtect, Prisma Access Agent, Enterprise DLP, AIOps, SaaS Security and AI Access Security, with Next-Generation Trust Security added in Q3 FY2026 as the eleventh. Each is a cloud service the firewall queries inline. Advanced Threat Prevention adds inline deep learning against command-and-control over HTTP, unknown-TCP, unknown-UDP and SSL; Advanced WildFire combines dynamic, static and recursive analysis and returns preventions in seconds (FY2025 10-K, Products and Services). The durable barrier is the inspection position, because training an inline detector requires inline traffic and the sensor fleet cannot be rented. The non-durable part is the detection content, which every incumbent also builds, and Microsoft bundles equivalent capability into E5 at a marginal price.

The attach depth is a longer menu as much as a deeper one. Per device sold, PANW reported 2.6 attached subscriptions of 4 attachable services in FY2016, about 65% of the menu. Per customer, 3.5 of 10 in FY2024, 35%. Per installed device, more than 4 of 11 in Q3 FY2026, about 36%. The count rose by more than half; the share of the available catalogue taken per unit is roughly half what it was. The three denominators differ and management has not bridged them, so the series cannot be chained.

Prisma Access, Prisma SD-WAN and Prisma Access Browser. Prisma Access is a cloud-delivered inspection fabric with more than 100 points of presence. Prisma SD-WAN, from CloudGenix, steers branch traffic across commodity broadband; Prisma Access Browser, from Talon, extends policy to unmanaged devices without an agent. Browser licences went from about 1 million in fiscal Q2 2025 to 11 million in Q3 FY2026. One qualifier on that count: on the fiscal Q1 2025 call the CEO said existing SASE customers "can deploy Prisma Access browser for their unused licenses," so licences issued and licences separately paid for are different numbers, and PANW discloses neither browser ARR nor deployed seats.

Precision AI. The brand PANW applies, from May 2024, to the machine-learning and deep-learning detection running inline in PAN-OS and the cloud-delivered services. Management's own account of why it is hard to copy is about data, not models: "as frontier models become available to everyone, the real competitive advantage shifts from model to the data fuel. That is why having sensors that sit in line with live traffic is so vital" (Q3 FY2026 call). The independent measurement that existed has ended. On 2025-09-12 PANW published that it "will not be participating in this year's MITRE evaluation," having decided to "adjust the focus of our engineering and testing resources," after two prior rounds of 100% technique-level detection (paloaltonetworks.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web]. Microsoft and SentinelOne also withdrew; eleven vendors participated, and CrowdStrike reported 100% detection, 100% protection and zero false positives in the same round (crowdstrike.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web]. Every current efficacy figure for the Cortex and Precision AI detection products, including the under-ten-minute median response time, is self-reported.

Cortex XSIAM. XSIAM ingests telemetry from endpoint, network, identity and cloud, correlates it and auto-triages, replacing a SIEM plus separate XDR, SOAR, network traffic analysis, attack-surface management and cloud detection and response. The economic hook is that a SIEM is priced on data ingested, so a platform that pre-analyses at ingest and routes cheaply changes the customer's cost curve.▪ Arora states the design intent directly: "we did design XSIAM with the idea of preanalyzing everything before we ingest the data" (Q3 FY2026 call). Displacing a SIEM means rewriting years of detection content and re-pointing every log source, which management prices at 12 to 18 months, and that is why the IBM QRadar asset purchase mattered: it supplied a named renewal list of more than 550 accounts.

Cortex Cloud and the Chronosphere Telemetry Pipeline. Cortex Cloud is a CNAPP merged with cloud detection and response, the successor to Prisma Cloud, which was itself assembled from Evident.io, RedLock, Twistlock, Bridgecrew, Cider and Dig. The Chronosphere Telemetry Pipeline, built on Calyptia, "acts as an intelligent control layer that filters, transforms, and routes data… reduce data volumes" (Q3 FY2026 10-Q). The same mechanism lowers PANW's own hosting cost per unit of customer-visible telemetry, which is why the acquisition was described as feeding XSIAM as much as serving observability buyers.

Idira. Launched May 2026 on CyberArk, covering privileged access, workforce identity, machine identity, governance and AI agent security. The one cross-platform proof point shipped so far is Next-Generation Trust Security, a certificate-lifecycle subscription built on CyberArk technology and sold as the eleventh firewall attach, which routes machine-identity demand through the network-security motion.

Where the technical position is exposed. Enforcement is moving off the standalone appliance and into the server. PANW runs Prisma AIRS on the NVIDIA BlueField DPU inside the NVIDIA Enterprise AI Factory validated design and has integrated Cortex XSIAM with NVIDIA DOCA Argus (paloaltonetworks.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web]. Cisco runs its Hybrid Mesh Firewall on the same BlueField DPUs at 400G line-rate stateful inspection in-server (blogs.cisco.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web]. In the AI data centre management named as the new appliance market, the acceleration silicon belongs to NVIDIA and is available to every competitor. The FE400 and FE100X ASICs do not participate. Hardware is about 10% of revenue, so the exposure is bounded in size.

Research and development was $1,984.1m in FY2025, 21.5% of revenue, and stepped to 24.5% in Q3 FY2026 as the acquired engineering teams consolidated. That funds a wider portfolio than either pure-play peer at a lower share of revenue than both: CrowdStrike spent about 29% of FY2026 revenue and Zscaler about 25% of FY2025 revenue on research and development, against Fortinet at about 13% [web].

3. Competitive advantages and moat assessment

Network Security

The Network Security advantage is a real installed-base annuity. It defends PANW's own revenue well and it converts into neither an excess margin nor compounding share.▪

The defensive half is documented. Roughly one million firewalls are deployed across more than 65,000 firewall customers, all running PAN-OS, the same operating system behind the VM-Series, CN-Series, Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access. More than four subscriptions are attached per installed device. Among the roughly 2,280 platformized accounts, net retention is 120% with single-digit churn.▪ A 10% hardware list increase implemented in April 2026 held, and management said it was evaluating further pricing actions. The book has also shifted decisively toward software: 46% of trailing product revenue was recurring software in Q3 FY2026 against 22% three years earlier, and the next-generation network security book of SASE plus software firewalls reached $3.9bn of ARR at fiscal 2025 year end, growing about 35%.

The conversion into economics weakens in two separate places.

Margin. FY2025 gross margin of 73.4% was 7.1 points below Fortinet's 80.5% and 13.3 points below Check Point's 86.7%, and GAAP operating margin of 13.5% was 17.2 points below Fortinet's 30.7%.▪ Gross margin in FY2025 matched FY2016's 73.2% on 6.7x the revenue, so a decade of volume produced no unit-cost leverage.▪ Mix does not explain the gap to Fortinet: re-weighting PANW to Fortinet's 32.6% / 67.4% product-and-service split at PANW's own line margins gives 74.0%, only 0.6 points above the 73.4% earned. The whole gap is in the recurring line, where PANW earned 72.5% against Fortinet's disclosed 86.8% service gross margin.▪ PANW runs Prisma Access on more than 100 of its own points of presence and pays for the compute that Fortinet and Check Point leave on the customer's appliance. It also spends 21.5% of revenue on research and development against Fortinet's 12.0% and Check Point's 16.8%, and after that spending earns lower margins than both. One consequence runs against the common framing: PANW's product gross margin exceeds its subscription and support gross margin, 77.1% against 72.5% in FY2025 and 71.9% against 66.5% in Q3 FY2026.▪

Share. In a four-vendor revenue pool of PANW, Fortinet, Check Point and Zscaler, PANW's total-revenue share rose 3.0 points between 2020 and 2025. Cortex grew from a small base to roughly a fifth of the company over the same span; adjusted for that, PANW's network-security-only share of the pool was between 1.4 points lower and 1.1 points higher in 2025 than in 2020.▪ The share that moved over five years is Check Point's, and Zscaler took most of it. In the most recent quarter, excluding the $388m CyberArk and Chronosphere contributed, PANW's pool share declined about a point from FY2025 while Fortinet's rose about 1.4 points and Zscaler's about 1.2.

The advantage is also contested on a known clock, which Arora describes from the attacking side: "we look forward to their refresh cycle so we get a chance to take out their customers and replace them with Palo Alto" (Q1 FY2025 call). Switching costs bind between refreshes and reopen at them, and PANW's own base refreshes on the same clock. In the two most recent comparable quarters the refresh went at least as much to the peer: Fortinet's product revenue grew 52% year over year to $773m in the June-2026 quarter against PANW's 31% to $594m in the April-2026 quarter, and the PANW figure includes CyberArk software licences.▪ External assessment moved the same way in the adjacent category: Gartner's 2026 SASE Platforms Magic Quadrant, reported 2026-08-03, placed PANW third behind Netskope and Cato, down from first▪, faulting the ION appliances' intrusion prevention and content filtering as "more constrained and cloud-reliant" (sdxcentral.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web].

This advantage earns its keep today, is defensible for now, and is open to erosion.▪ PANW is not price-taking: 120% net retention in the platformized cohort, a 10% hardware increase that held, and a 77.1% product gross margin against Fortinet's 67.3% are not commodity behaviour. Nor has it survived a well-funded attack while throwing off excess returns with little reinvestment: it outspends both incumbent rivals on research and development by a wide margin and still earns less than either, and its network-security share of the peer pool has not grown in five years once the Cortex mix shift is stripped out.

Test by test.

Claimed source The test it must pass What the evidence shows
Switching costs Retention and renewal pricing Partly present. 120% net retention with single-digit churn, but only for the roughly 2,280 platformized accounts, a cohort defined by having already consolidated. Company-wide retention is undisclosed, and support revenue growth decelerated to 9.4% in FY2025 from 13.0%
Pricing power Realised price outrunning input-cost inflation Present and unresolved. A 10% hardware list increase landed in April 2026 with further actions under evaluation, and Gartner cites PANW's pricing as expensive relative to SASE rivals. Against that, Q3 FY2026 hardware gross margin declined in the quarter the increase landed
Scale A unit-cost or margin gap widening with volume Absent. Gross margin 73.2% in FY2016 and 73.4% in FY2025 on 6.7x the revenue; the gap to Fortinet is unchanged at roughly 7 points over five years
Installed base and attach Attach compounding on a growing base Present. Roughly 1m firewalls, more than 65,000 firewall customers, more than 4 subscriptions per device, recurring software from 22% to 46% of trailing product revenue in three years
One operating system across form factors Cross-sell from the firewall base into SASE and software firewalls Present. SASE ARR $1.6bn +40%, software firewall ARR +25%, next-generation network security ARR $3.9bn +35% at FY2025 year end, roughly 50 SASE displacement wins worth $200m of contract value in nine months. The cost is the recurring gross margin, 14 points below Fortinet's
Data and threat telemetry A detection advantage showing in win rates or price Not demonstrated. Roughly 1m inline firewalls is a plausible input; no win-rate, pricing or renewal series exists to test the output
Distribution Channel reach converting to share Neutral. More than 8,500 NextWave partners and four cloud marketplaces, and Fortinet names the same four distributors PANW's trade press names
Cost position A manufacturing or silicon cost advantage Against PANW. Fortinet designs its own silicon; PANW uses Flex with merchant components, sole-source integrated circuits, no capacity or pricing guarantee, and a newly disclosed memory shortage
Brand and category recognition Third-party category leadership Mixed. Leader in hybrid mesh firewalls and first on completeness of vision there; third in SASE Platforms in 2026, down from first

Cortex

Cortex earns high returns on each incremental sale and has not returned its cost of capital on the money that built it. The asset producing the incremental sale belongs to Network Security.▪

The incremental economics are unusual. XSIAM reached 740 customers within 42 months of general availability, paying more than $600m of ARR between them, sold by a field organisation the firewall business already funds. Arora described the distribution asset precisely when discussing Chronosphere at the UBS conference on 2025-12-02: "They have 7 salespeople, I have 3,000." Landing eight-figure security-operations commitments inside accounts that already buy firewalls is a channel result.

The all-in economics are weak. PANW assembled the three Cortex legs by buying fifteen businesses and asset packages for roughly $7.4bn of booked purchase consideration, about $7.1bn after the IBM QRadar earn-out markdowns, against an estimated $2.4bn-$2.8bn of Cortex ARR at 2026-04-30 [estimate: the FY2024 disclosed components of $900m of Cortex ARR plus $700m of cloud-security ARR, grown at the disclosed "nearly 25%" for FY2025 and then at the organic NGS rate of 28% annualised for nine months, plus Chronosphere at above $300m; the range reflects the "passed"/"first to" wording of the base figures]. A 20% operating margin, above Dynatrace's 12.2% at $2.0bn of revenue and above Datadog's −1.3% at $3.4bn, produces $340m-$400m of after-tax profit at PANW's FY2025 effective rate of 28.9%, which is 4.6%-5.6% on the purchase price before any organic research spending, against a hurdle near 9-10% for a company financed almost entirely with equity.▪ Both directions of error make that generous: the margin exceeds every comparable at that scale, and the capital base excludes the engineering PANW funded itself.

The durability test has run once and Cortex lost it. Cloud security was the first leg to meet a well-funded specialist.▪ PANW last gave a cloud-security ARR figure of more than $700m for the year ended 2024-07-31, calling itself then "the largest pure-play cybersecurity cloud security business being the first to $700 million in ARR." Wiz reached roughly the same scale over the same window and Alphabet completed its acquisition on 2026-03-11 (googlecloudpresscorner.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web]; the widely reported price is $32bn all-cash (forbes.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web]. Arora volunteered the diagnosis on the Q3 FY2025 call: "we learned our lesson in cloud. In cloud security, we dwell too long on the peace time capabilities of cloud security or the posture capabilities of Prisma Cloud." Prisma Cloud was rebuilt as Cortex Cloud in February 2025 and the ARR line has not been given since.

Two things inside the Cortex numbers move against the moat argument. Combined Cortex and Cloud ARR grew "nearly 25%" year over year in Q4 FY2025 while XSIAM roughly doubled over the same twelve months, which leaves the rest of Cortex — XDR, XSOAR, Xpanse and the cloud portfolio — growing about 10% on a base near $1.4bn▪ [estimate: combined ARR of ~$1.60bn at 2024-07-31 and ~$2.00bn at 2025-07-31 less XSIAM at ~$0.15bn and ~$0.41bn; the deck's own $1.7bn combined figure at 2025-07-31 puts the residual base nearer $1.2bn and the growth rate in the same low-double-digit band]. And the average XSIAM customer is getting smaller: above $1.0m of ARR at roughly 400 customers in Q4 FY2025, "nearly $1 million" at more than 600 in Q2 FY2026, and about $811k across 740 in Q3 FY2026.▪

The cost side moves the wrong way as the data claim gets bigger. Management's central technical claim is that XSIAM processes more than 17 petabytes of daily telemetry, "volume unmatched by any other pure-play security vendor." The same volume is the cost base; Arora told the UBS conference PANW was "possibly the top 5 customers of BigQuery at Google." GAAP subscription and support gross margin declined from 73.4% in FY2024 to 72.5% in FY2025, which the 10-K attributes "primarily due to an increase in costs related to our cloud-based offerings." Datadog runs an 80.0% gross margin and Dynatrace 81.6%; PANW's services book runs 72.5% GAAP and 75.1% on management's non-GAAP basis.

Cortex earns excess returns on the incremental sale today and is defensible for the twelve to eighteen months a security-operations deployment takes to unwind, and it is open to erosion by three attackers who reach the same buyer through a channel of comparable strength.▪ Arora priced the switching cost himself at the Citi conference on 2025-09-04: "you can't replace a network security platform from Palo Alto in under 3 years if you are fully platformized across the board or you can't replace a SIEM platform in less than 12 to 18 months if you are fully platformized." That makes the Cortex lock-in roughly half the depth of the Network Security lock-in, on contracts averaging about three years.

Identity Security (Idira)

The identity franchise holds a real switching cost at the level of the installed credential vault, and that switching cost is the part of the moat supported without qualification.▪ PANW assigned $3,500m of the $21,061m purchase price — 56% of all identified intangibles — to platform renewals amortised over 12 to 14 years, against $219m for the in-place contract backlog over two years (Q3 FY2026 10-Q, Note 7).▪ A thirteen-year renewal life implies annual attrition near 8%. CyberArk was named a Leader in Gartner's Privileged Access Management Magic Quadrant for a seventh consecutive cycle in October 2025 and positioned furthest in completeness of vision (cyberark.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web]. Revenue compounded from $464m in 2020 to $1,361m in 2025, 24.0% a year, and total ARR reached $1,440m at 2025-12-31.

That position has not converted into excess returns. Adding back all $115.8m of amortisation of acquired intangibles but still charging the $234.4m of share-based compensation, CyberArk's 2025 operating margin was −1.1% on $1,361.1m of revenue.▪ It has reported a GAAP operating loss in every year since 2021. Okta, whose dollar-based net retention is 106% and whose franchise nobody describes as sticky, earned a positive 5.1% GAAP operating margin in the year ended 2026-01-31 and a 30.0% free cash flow margin, against CyberArk's 19.0%. The two charge similar stock compensation, 18.6% of revenue at Okta and 17.2% at CyberArk. Two decades after inventing the category and seven Gartner cycles as its leader, the privileged-access franchise does not out-earn the access-management vendor beside it.

The industry structure explains why. Microsoft lists Entra ID P2, which includes Privileged Identity Management, at $10.00 per user per month and includes it at no incremental charge with Microsoft 365 E5▪ (microsoft.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web]. CyberArk's entire 2025 revenue spread across the 8 million privileged-access users management cited in the deal deck gives a maximum of $170 per user per year, and the true privileged seat price is below that because Venafi machine identity, Zilla governance and the workforce products are inside the same $1,361m. Management's case for the acquisition depends on pushing privilege controls from 8 million seats to "hundreds of millions" (Arora, M&A call, 2025-07-30), and most of those seats already own a bundled substitute. Separately, Okta bought a working cloud-native privileged-access platform, Axiom Security, on 2025-09-04 for $54m in cash, of which it allocated $16m to developed technology (Okta 10-Q for the quarter ended 2025-10-31, Note 6). Working technology cost $16m; the installed base cost PANW $3,500m of platform-renewals intangible plus $2,537m of developed technology.

On the capital PANW committed, identity currently returns about 1%. Capital deployed is $20,404m: $21,061m of consideration plus $1,303m of assumed convertible notes, less $743m of acquired cash and $1,217m of acquired investments. CyberArk's non-GAAP operating income run-rate entering the deal was about $300m a year, which at its own 24% non-GAAP tax rate is $228m, or 1.1% on that capital. For identity to earn 8% after tax it needs $1,632m of after-tax operating profit, which at PANW's 27.1% non-GAAP operating margin and a 20% tax rate requires roughly $7.5bn of identity revenue against a current run-rate near $1.5bn — about seven years at 25% annual growth or nine at 20%. Cross-sell into PANW's 70,000 core customers shows up in the network-security and Cortex lines, so a strict segment computation understates the case; it does not change the order of magnitude.

This is an advantage that is defensible today and open to erosion. It is not in the class of positions that have survived well-funded attempts to break them: Microsoft, Okta and SailPoint are all attacking it now, and the attack has already compressed the economics to the point where a category leader runs at breakeven.▪ Nor is it commodity competition, because an attacker cannot take a deployed vault away by cutting price, which is what the twelve-to-fourteen-year renewal life prices in.

Return on invested capital

Basis. ROIC in the ten-year table below is after-tax GAAP operating income at a flat 21% rate, divided by the average of opening and closing invested capital measured gross of customer float: equity plus convertible notes plus operating lease liabilities, less cash and investments, plus total deferred revenue, less balance-sheet deferred tax assets. Invested capital net of customer float subtracts total deferred revenue from that figure. The 21% rate is used because the GAAP effective rate was negative in eight of the ten years and −160.8% in FY2024 on the valuation-allowance release.

Two measures point different ways. On capital gross of customer float — the assets management must fund before customer prepayments count — ROIC crossed zero only in FY2023 and reached 10.3% in FY2025. Seven of the ten years are negative and none clears a mid-teens hurdle. On capital net of float, invested capital was negative in eight of the ten years and minus $2,641m in FY2025: total deferred revenue of $12,751.9m is 26% larger than the $10,111.3m base it funds.▪ Rolling three-year incremental returns were negative from FY2017-FY2020 through FY2019-FY2022 and then improved to 11.6%, 23.6% and 31.6%. Whether that persists through the CyberArk capital is the open question: the deal added $21.1bn of invested capital in one quarter, roughly twice the entire FY2025 base, against $388m of quarterly revenue and a $523m quarterly operating loss.

4. Competitive landscape and market sizing

Network security

Dell'Oro measured global network security revenue above $26bn for full-year 2025, growing 9%, and projects the market to approach $29bn in 2026, with SSE up 20% inside 2025, web application firewalls up 12% and firewalls in the single digits (delloro.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web]. The hardware line then inflected: Dell'Oro's August 2026 forecast puts network security hardware above $90bn cumulatively over 2025-2030, a 7% compound rate against 3.8% realised over 2020-2025, with firewalls exceeding $20bn by 2030 (delloro.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web]. SASE was above $3bn in 1Q 2026, up 21%, roughly $12bn annualised (delloro.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web].

Rebuilt bottom-up from each vendor's own filings, PANW at $6.9-7.4bn of FY2025 network-security revenue, Fortinet at $6.0-6.5bn, Check Point at $2,725m, Zscaler at $2,673m, Cisco at $2.6-3.0bn, Netskope at $709m and Cato above $350m of ARR total roughly $22-23bn against the $26bn measured. The two definitions do not line up: Dell'Oro includes application delivery controllers and web application firewalls where PANW barely competes, which widens its denominator, and the vendor column includes PANW's $2,445.2m of support revenue, some of which may fall outside the research house's scope. PANW's share of measured network security is 26-29% [estimate: $6.9-7.4bn of FY2025 revenue against a $26bn denominator; on the current run-rate, 70% of Q3 FY2026 revenue annualises to $8.4bn against a market approaching $29bn, or 29%]. The direction is better established than the level.

Dell'Oro's last published vendor split for the firewall segment covers 2Q 2024: combined physical and virtual firewall revenue of $3.2bn, up 1.5%, split $2.8bn physical (down 1%) and $420m virtual (up 22%), with PANW at 29% and Cisco and Fortinet at 15% each▪ (cybersecuritydive.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web].

Unit share and revenue share point opposite ways. Ken Xie described Fortinet in February 2026 as "the #1 firewall leader with a 55% unit market share" (Fortinet Q4 2025 earnings release). Fortinet therefore earns 15% of firewall revenue on 55% of units, about 0.27x the market average revenue per unit.▪ PANW earns 29% of revenue on a unit share that cannot exceed 45% and is plausibly 8-15% given how much of the volume tail is small-business and branch, implying 1.9-3.6x the market average, or 7-13x Fortinet's [estimate: 29% revenue share divided by an 8-15% assumed unit share, against Fortinet's 15% divided by its stated 55%; the unit-share assumption is the estimate and both revenue shares and Fortinet's unit share are stated figures, from different quarters]. The two leaders sell into different parts of the same market.

Over the decade Check Point gave up 26.2 points of the pool. PANW took 12.3, Zscaler 10.7 and Fortinet 3.2.▪ Since 2022, when Check Point's donation slowed, PANW gained 1.9 points, Zscaler 4.3 and Fortinet lost 1.4. Five-year revenue growth to 2025: Zscaler 44.0%, PANW 22.0%, Fortinet 21.3%, Check Point 5.7%.

Share counter-evidence, ranked by how much each changes the market structure.

  1. Fortinet is winning the current refresh on volume, price and margin at once. Product revenue +41% then +52% in the last two quarters, driven by "higher unit shipments year over year, higher average selling prices resulting from customer demand for higher-performing models and recent pricing actions" (Fortinet 10-Q). Total revenue growth accelerated to 26% against PANW's 14% organic. Product gross margin expanded 240 basis points while PANW's compressed 590.
  2. Fortinet is attacking the architectural claim directly. Its Q2 2026 release describes "Fortinet's unique 'SASE Firewall', with leading firewall, SD-WAN and SASE functionality integrated together on our single FortiOS operating system and powered by our purpose-built FortiASIC" — PANW's own claim, with a silicon advantage attached and an Intel co-development programme behind the next processor generation.
  3. Geography. Fortinet earned $871.7m in EMEA in the June-2026 quarter against PANW's $633m in the April-2026 quarter, and $368.0m in APAC against $351m, with PANW's figures inflated by acquisitions. Full-year mixes: PANW Americas 67% / EMEA 21% / APAC 12%; Fortinet 40 / 42 / 18; Check Point 42 / 46 / 12. PANW's leadership in network security is a North American position.
  4. Zscaler's absolute lead in SSE keeps widening. Zscaler's ARR was $3,525m at 2026-04-30 growing 25%; PANW's SASE ARR was $1.6bn growing 40%. At those rates Zscaler adds roughly $710-880m of ARR a year against PANW's $640m, so the dollar gap widens from about $1.9bn to about $2.2bn over the next twelve months.▪
  5. The hyperscalers. PANW has named Microsoft as a competitor since FY2023 and Alphabet since FY2024, and the Q3 FY2026 10-Q warns that "larger vendors, including the cloud hyperscalers and other cybersecurity companies with specialized or broad platforms, may meaningfully enter or further expand into additional cybersecurity categories."
  6. Component supply. Both PANW and Fortinet disclosed a memory shortage in their most recent 10-Qs and both are raising hardware prices. PANW's stated mitigation is that "our acquired component volumes are not as significant to some of our peers," which says it buys fewer components, and in an allocation-constrained market the smaller buyer has the weaker claim.
  7. Check Point is close to fully donated. Its share of the pool went from 38.9% in 2016 to 12.7% in 2025 to 10.9% on the latest quarter, now smaller than Zscaler's.

Security operations, cloud security and observability

Third-party sizing of the SIEM market runs to $8.39bn in 2026 growing to $13.67bn by 2031, a 10.3% compound rate (marketsandmarkets.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web]. Management's own figure was "the entire $20 billion TAM of SIEM" on the Q1 FY2025 call and a "$40 billion SecOps TAM" two quarters later. A bottom-up build from what vendors disclose lands near the syndicated number: Cisco's Splunk security book at roughly $2.4bn [estimate: Splunk total ARR of $4.2bn at 2024-01-31, of which security has historically been the larger of two solution books], PANW's XSIAM at $0.6bn, IBM's residual on-premise QRadar at roughly $500m (an analyst figure on the PANW Q1 FY2025 call, uncorrected by management), SentinelOne's $1.2bn of mostly-endpoint ARR, and an unsized Microsoft Sentinel contribution. Adding those gets to $7-10bn, about half management's $20bn. The $40bn figure holds only on a definition that folds in endpoint protection, managed detection and response, orchestration, attack-surface management and threat intelligence, most of which XSIAM does not address today.

The two challengers added roughly $540m of combined next-generation SIEM ARR in the year to April 2026 against a market third parties size at $8-12bn, so about 5% of the market moved to the two of them in a year, while Cisco's entire security product line declined $136m across nine months. Displacement is real and slow, and the incumbent shrinks by less each year than the challengers add, so the pool is growing too. The two labels cover different things: CrowdStrike labels its line "LogScale Next-Gen SIEM," so it includes log management, while PANW's excludes Cortex XDR and the Telemetry Pipeline. Neither is audited and neither vendor publishes the composition.

In cloud security PANW went from a book larger than Wiz's in mid-2024, above $700m of ARR against roughly $500m, to third.▪ Wiz passed $1bn during 2025 and Alphabet closed its acquisition on 2026-03-11; PANW has published no cloud-security level for seven quarters and estimates put it at $760m-$895m [estimate: $700m at 2024-07-31 compounded at 5-15% for 1.75 years, the lower bound assuming the cloud book absorbed the whole of the drag management described]. This is the clearest share loss in the portfolio, and it happened in the sub-market with the most third-party validation of demand.

In observability PANW enters at roughly one fifteenth of Datadog's run rate. Datadog reported $1,121m of revenue in the quarter ended 2026-06-30, up 35.6%, with 33,400 customers and net retention in the low 120s; Dynatrace had $2,054m of ARR at 2026-03-31, up 18%; Elastic had $1,739m of FY2026 revenue across three solutions; Grafana Labs passed $400m of ARR with more than 7,000 customers [web]. Chronosphere was above $300m of ARR at 2026-04-30, and PANW paid $2,951m of recorded consideration for a business at above $160m of ARR at announcement, about 18x.

Identity security

Gartner's 2025 Privileged Access Management Magic Quadrant puts PAM market revenue for 2025 at $3.25bn, growing 12%, across twelve evaluated vendors with CyberArk, BeyondTrust and Delinea as the only Leaders (research.oz.spotlightar.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web]. Stepping out to the end-customer dollar needs the two channel layers. Distributor gross margin is sourced: 6.99% at TD SYNNEX in fiscal 2025, 6.67% at Ingram Micro, and 11.4% on Arrow's Global ECS segment, the closest comparison because it distributes enterprise IT. The reseller layer is not disclosed anywhere available. Holding the distributor band at 7-11% and varying the reseller margin between 10% and 25% puts PANW's own capture at $0.67 to $0.84 of the end-customer dollar.▪ Two routes bypass the channel: the cloud marketplaces charge 3% on SaaS listings, banding to 1.5% above $10m of contract value at AWS [web], and PANW's direct sales force negotiates the large platform deals itself with the reseller fulfilling.

The binding constraint is compute. Non-cancelable commitments have moved decisively.

Cloud commitments grew 5.3x between 2023-07-31 and 2026-04-30 while revenue grew about 1.6x; the FY2023 line was labelled "other purchase commitments with certain service providers" before PANW split Cloud out from FY2024, so the two labels are not the same disclosure. Manufacturing commitments have never exceeded $360m and none of the current $246m falls beyond FY2027. PANW owes $8,092m of minimum cloud purchases, $3,598m of it in fiscal 2031 and beyond, and the 10-Q allocates none of it to a platform.

The physical constraint applies to a small base, and that base is growing fast. Global DRAM contract prices rose 90-95% quarter over quarter in Q1 calendar 2026 and 58-63% in Q2, with NAND up 70-75% in Q2 (trendforce.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web]. The Q3 FY2026 10-Q added new language: "there is currently a global shortage of memory-related components, which are a component in certain of our products." Hardware is about 10% of revenue, so hardware ran near $300m in the April quarter; memory and storage at 10-20% of a networking-appliance bill of materials is $9-21m of quarterly cost, and a doubling of prices adds the same again [estimate: the 10-20% memory share of the bill of materials is the weak input and is disclosed by neither PANW nor a comparable]. The 10% April 2026 hardware price increase is worth roughly $30m a quarter once the order book turns over, so the pass-through covers the top of the estimated cost range. Non-GAAP product gross margin was 78.8% in Q3 FY2026, up 40 basis points year over year, through the worst of the memory move; the GAAP figure declined 5.9 points on amortisation.

Customer-side economics. PANW served approximately 70,000 customers with roughly one million firewalls, and trailing revenue at 2026-04-30 was $10,607m, so average revenue per customer was roughly $150,000. Per installed firewall, network security generated roughly $7,400 a year of which roughly $1,100 was hardware, so every dollar of firewall hardware shipped returns about six dollars of annual network-security subscription and support [estimate: management's ~70% Network Security share and ~10% hardware share applied to trailing revenue, over the one-million install base]. The same arithmetic gives roughly 160,000 units shipped a year into a one-million base at a blended $6,900 average selling price, a six-year replacement cycle; at $5,000 it is four to five years and at $10,000 nine.

At the platform end the customer commitment is much larger. Three fiscal Q4 2025 platformization wins ran $111m, $61m and $33m of deal value against NGS ARR of $50m, $15m and $12m at those same customers (Q4 FY2025 deck, slide 7). At Q4 FY2025 PANW had 156 customers above $5m of NGS ARR, up 51%, and 51 above $10m, up 50%; by Q3 FY2026 it was 195 and 67, both up about 50%. Sixty-seven customers above $10m is at least $670m of ARR, roughly 8% of the $8,130m NGS ARR, held by 0.1% of the customer base.

Bargaining power, interface by interface.

  • Component suppliers to PANW: moving against PANW. No volume purchase contracts, prices that change frequently, and DRAM contract prices that roughly tripled across the first half of calendar 2026. PANW extended manufacturing commitments into a second fiscal year for the first time since FY2024 — manufacturing commitments falling beyond twelve months were nil at 2025-07-31, $22m at 2026-01-31 and $152m at 2026-04-30 — and raised its own prices 10% within one quarter.
  • Flex to PANW: static, and small on both sides. Flex billings are an estimated $227m-$289m in FY2025, 0.8-1.0% of Flex's $27.9bn of fiscal 2026 revenue, on which Flex earns roughly 5.4%, about $12m-$16m of segment income. Neither side can hurt the other through price; the exposure is operational, because a switch of manufacturing partner would delay deliveries.
  • PANW to cloud providers: moving against PANW, and PANW is paying to fix it. Cloud commitments rose $1,646m in the April 2026 quarter alone. On 2025-12-19 PANW and Google Cloud announced a "multibillion-dollar agreement" under which PANW migrates key internal workloads to Google Cloud (paloaltonetworks.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web]. That counterparty is also a competitor: both the FY2025 10-K and the Q3 FY2026 10-Q name Alphabet, Alphabet owns Wiz, and the same company sells PANW compute, resells PANW software, and competes with Cortex.
  • PANW to distributors: moving toward PANW. Distributor agreements have a one-year initial term, one-year renewals, termination by PANW on 30 to 90 days' notice, and payment within 30 to 45 days. Dependence is asymmetric even at 44.2%: PANW's whole FY2025 revenue would be 15% of TD SYNNEX's $62,508m and 18% of Ingram Micro's roughly $52.5bn, so each of the three took roughly 3% of its own sales from PANW while supplying PANW with 11-19% of its revenue.
  • PANW to end customers: split by deal size. Golechha on the Q2 FY2025 call: "really where you see the majority of the requests for deferred payments is in the higher end… And on firewall, we typically get the money upfront because that's being budgeted based on a refresh cycle." Small deals settle upfront through the distributor's balance sheet; large deals draw payment terms from PANW's.

Circular financing. PANW finances qualified end customers and channel partners directly on two-to-five-year terms and keeps the credit risk, selling only paper rated 5 or worse. The book is shrinking hard: gross financing receivables were $2,116.6m at 2024-07-31 (26.4% of revenue), $1,885.5m at 2025-07-31 (20.4%) and $1,495m at 2026-04-30 (14.1% of trailing revenue), and PANW sold $37.8m of receivables in FY2025, 2.0% of the gross book. Set against that, half of guided FY2026 free cash flow is collection on bookings already made: Golechha said on the Q4 FY2025 call that PANW "had visibility to approximately 40% of that free cash flow from deferred payments on deals signed prior to the fiscal year" and expects "about half of our fiscal '26 free cash flow to come from deferred payment deals signed in fiscal '25 or earlier."

6. Secular and industry trends

The binding quantity for roughly 80% of PANW revenue is the enterprise security budget.▪ Gartner puts worldwide information security end-user spending at $193bn in 2024, $213bn in 2025 and $244bn in 2026, growing 10.4% then 14.6%, and forecasts a 10.0% constant-currency compound rate from 2024 to 2029 [web]. Anything PANW earns above that rate is share taken from another vendor. Two mechanisms could lift security's share of the IT budget itself: inline inspection volume from AI traffic, which both PANW and Dell'Oro name and neither publishes a series for, and machine identities, where privileged access grows at 22-24% against identity and access management at 10-12%.

The step to 31% in the April 2026 quarter is entirely purchased.▪ There was one deceleration event, and it happened inside fiscal 2024: quarterly revenue growth went from +26% to +12% across four quarters, coinciding with the platformization pivot announced on 2024-02-20. Against the ultimate volume drivers. Every platform line grows faster than its own market: SASE ARR +40% against a Dell'Oro SASE market at +21%; software firewall ARR +25% against a software and SaaS-delivered network security market Dell'Oro puts near 15% compound to 2029; XSIAM ARR about +100% against SIEM at 10-12%; hardware NGFW bookings about +40% against a firewall market growing at single digits.▪ The consolidated organic result is +14%, three to four points above the market, because the fast lines are small and the slow-growing installed base of attached subscriptions and support is large at 43% of revenue.

Matching PANW's July fiscal year to the calendar market gives an organic share of worldwide security spending of about 4.5% in FY2025 and about 4.6% in FY2026; the acquisitions added about 0.4 points [estimate: FY2025 revenue of $9,221.5m against the average of CY2024 $193bn and CY2025 $213bn; FY2026 organic revenue of ~$10.5bn against the average of CY2025 $213bn and CY2026 $244bn]. Over one year PANW at 14.9% and Fortinet at 14.2% are within a point of each other; over five years, 22.0% against 21.3%. The gap opens only over three years. Every cloud-native security vendor in the table grew faster than PANW in the latest year, including four that are a third of PANW's size or smaller, and the fastest grower in the cohort at +36.0% was CyberArk, which PANW then bought.

The claimed secular driver. Consolidation onto one vendor did appear in the numbers, in the forward book and not in revenue. Net retention among platformized customers is 119-120% with low single-digit churn, organic RPO grew 22% and organic current RPO 17% while organic revenue grew 14%. Consolidation is showing up as longer and larger commitments from customers PANW already has, and in the nine quarters since the strategy launched it has not moved the consolidated organic revenue rate above the mid-teens. One figure makes the same point from the other side: the Q3 FY2026 10-Q's own pro forma combination of PANW, Chronosphere and CyberArk, as though all three had been owned from the start of fiscal 2025, grew 17.4% over nine months and 16.1% in the quarter, against PANW's standalone organic 14.9%. Roughly $24.0bn of purchase consideration moved the like-for-like growth rate of the whole enterprise by about two and a half points.▪

Cyclical versus secular

The cyclical share of the business has halved: hardware is about 10% of revenue against about 20% in FY2021. Product revenue is a poor proxy for it after fiscal 2024, because 46% of trailing product revenue is now recurring software and the FY2025 10-K attributes part of the product line's growth to "an increase in price of, and allocation to, on-premise software licenses."

The hardware cycle is at or near a peak, and management disclosed all three things underneath the Q3 FY2026 result. A new appliance generation entered volume in fiscal 2026. A 10% list price increase took effect in early April 2026, one month before the quarter closed on 30 April, which contributes to bookings directly and creates an incentive to order ahead of it. And Dell'Oro raised its network security hardware forecast to a 7% compound rate for 2025-2030 from 3.8% realised, attributing it to "AI infrastructure investment and risk-led refresh cycles." A firewall market growing at single digits does not produce 40% growth for its largest vendor on trend alone. The 10% price rise puts a ceiling on how much of the 40% can be volume: at most about 30 points, and some of that is the generation change and order timing.

The AI-linked revenue is real, small and concentrated. Prisma AIRS reached more than 300 customers from about 100 one quarter earlier, with management describing "clear visibility towards $100 million in ARR over the next couple of quarters." Observability ARR passed $300m, up more than half in a quarter, with the increase attributed to one existing LLM customer and a single frontier AI lab above $200m of ARR. That spending is funded by AI training and inference capital expenditure.

Source: Q1 FY2026 earnings deck, slide 14, footnoted to sources shared at the Q4 FY2023 call. Between fiscal 2018 and the fiscal 2026 guidance PANW's revenue grew about 5.0x, from $2,273.6m to $11.42bn; the stated addressable market grew about 11x to its 2025 figure and about 15x to its 2028 figure. Management's penetration figure therefore declined as the company grew: "low double-digit market share… in about a $20 billion total addressable market" on the Q3 FY2018 call, "north of $200 billion" at the Goldman conference in September 2023, and "less than 5% penetrated into a TAM, reaching nearly $300 billion in the next 3 years" on the Q1 FY2026 call.

Two of the four blocks can be checked against third-party measurement. Removing the SSE overlap, a Dell'Oro-based firewall-plus-SASE market is roughly $22-25bn [estimate: the firewall segment at ~$13bn annualised from the last published quarterly figure grown at Dell'Oro's stated single-digit rate, plus ~$12bn of SASE, less the SSE double-count], so PANW's $59bn is 2.4-2.7x it. And the $93bn SOC-plus-Cloud figure is more than 3x a SIEM market third parties size at $8-12bn plus a cloud-security market whose disclosed vendor ARR totals under $3bn. The growth rate inside the slide is more defensible than the level: $59bn to $80bn over three years is 10.6% a year, and Dell'Oro forecasts firewalls at nearly double digits and SSE at 16% over 2025-2030.▪

The $79bn added to the 2028 figure between the $210bn network-and-SOC total and the ~$289bn total is exactly the identity and observability categories PANW entered by acquisition in the same two quarters.

Q1 FY2026 (Nov 2025) $20bn —
Q3 FY2026 (Jun 2026) $20bn "surpassing 4,000"

The $5bn increase was announced on the call that announced the two acquisitions, and CyberArk and Chronosphere had already supplied $1.63bn of NGS ARR by Q3 FY2026. Compounding that at CyberArk's own roughly 30% subscription-ARR growth for four years gives about $4.7bn against a $5bn raise, so the acquired books account for the raise and the organic ambition did not move.▪ Reaching $20bn from the FY2026 guided exit of $8.90-8.95bn requires 22.4% compound growth for four years and average net new NGS ARR near $2.8bn a year, against organic net new NGS ARR of $370m in Q3 FY2026 and roughly $1.4bn across the four quarters to 2026-04-30.▪ The platformization half is milder: 4,000 from about 2,280 needs roughly 101 net additions a quarter for 17 quarters against 110 delivered in Q3 FY2026 and a disclosed range of about 60 to 150 across the nine quarters PANW has given.▪ What has to rise at the same time is NGS ARR per platformization, from $3.6m to $5.0m, about 8% a year.

7. Critical points

1. The largest revenue line in the company is the one PANW never sizes, and it moves the forward answer more than any other. Attached subscriptions and support is about $4,926m, 43% of FY2026 revenue, and it grew roughly 7% in FY2026.▪ Two percentage points a year on it changes fiscal 2035 free cash flow by $494m in the base case, against $355m for SASE ARR, $104m for hardware and $96m for observability. It is visible only as a residual after product, SASE, Cortex and identity are removed from total revenue, and it absorbs the entire error in the Unit 42 estimate of $200-400m. Management's disclosure runs the other way: observability, XSIAM and the hardware quarter get named figures every call.

2. Growth stopped decelerating two years ago, and the level is mid-teens. Organic revenue growth ran 13.9%, 14.3%, 15.3%, 15.8%, 15.7%, 14.9% and 14.2% across the seven quarters from Q1 FY2025 to Q3 FY2026. The one deceleration event was fiscal 2024, from +26% to +12% across four quarters, tied to the February 2024 platformization pivot, and it did not repeat. Organic current remaining performance obligations grew 17% in Q3 FY2026, up from 15% in Q2, running about three points ahead of organic revenue. That runs against a bear case built on continuing deceleration and against a bull case built on acceleration.

3. About $24.0bn of purchase consideration moved combined like-for-like growth by two and a half points. The Q3 FY2026 10-Q's own pro forma combination of PANW, Chronosphere and CyberArk grew 17.4% over nine months and 16.1% in the quarter, against PANW's standalone organic 14.9% and 14.2%. Against the standalone FY2026 plan management published on 2025-11-19, consolidating the two acquisitions added about $0.9bn of revenue, lowered the guided non-GAAP operating margin midpoint by 70 basis points, lowered the guided adjusted free cash flow margin by 100 basis points, lowered guided non-GAAP EPS by $0.07 and raised the guided share count by 7.2%.

4. The moat is bought, and the efficiency it creates has gone to the customer. PANW spends 21.5% of revenue on research and development against Fortinet's 12.0% and Check Point's 16.8%, and it absorbs the delivery cost of running security from its own cloud, worth about 14 points of gross margin on 80% of revenue.▪ Both are the price of the consolidation strategy that produces 120% net retention in the platformized cohort. FY2025 gross margin of 73.4% matched FY2016's 73.2% on 6.7x the revenue, and the gap to Fortinet's gross margin has not moved in five years.

5. Cortex earns high returns on the incremental sale and has not returned its cost of capital on the money that built it. Roughly $7.1bn of effective purchase consideration across fifteen transactions supports an estimated $2.4-$2.8bn of ARR. At a 20% operating margin, above Dynatrace at $2.0bn of revenue and Datadog at $3.4bn, that returns 4.6-5.6% against a 9-10% hurdle. The advantage producing the incremental sale belongs to Network Security: "They have 7 salespeople, I have 3,000," as Arora described Chronosphere at the UBS conference. Cloud security is the completed experiment on how far the firewall base transfers: PANW spent $1,621m across eight deals, reached $700m of ARR by July 2024, and has published no level since while Wiz passed $1bn and sold to Alphabet.

6. The share count moves free cash flow per share more than any operating driver, and it is the line PANW has managed worst. One percentage point a year on the diluted count is worth $1.09 of fiscal 2035 free cash flow per share in the model, nearly double the largest revenue driver. Over FY2016-FY2025 the split-adjusted basic count rose 26.8% while $5,108m of repurchases retired 120.4m shares against gross issuance near 260m, so the buyback absorbed 46% of issuance. In February 2026 PANW issued 112m shares for CyberArk and repurchased 6.8m, a net expansion of 105m shares, 15.9% of the FY2025 average count.

7. Two-thirds of the fastest-growing platform may be one customer. Observability ARR passed $300m at Q3 FY2026, up more than 50% from $200m one quarter earlier, and the CFO attributed the step to "an existing LLM customer increasing consumption as they continue to migrate from the incumbent vendor." The same call reports surpassing "$200 million in ARR with a leading frontier AI lab." Both figures are "over" figures, so the ratio between them is a range: one customer is between a third and roughly two-thirds of the leg, and PANW does not split the $200m between observability and other platforms. Pricing is usage-based and contracted remaining performance obligations were about $150m against $200m of ARR at 2026-01-31, under one year of coverage.

8. Fixed cloud commitments now dwarf every other contractual obligation. Non-cancelable cloud purchases were $8,092m at 2026-04-30 against $1,097m of debt principal, $778m of lease liabilities and $246m of manufacturing commitments. The annual steps run $449m in FY2027, $1,295m in FY2028, $1,352m in FY2029 and $1,398m in FY2030, with $3,598m in fiscal 2031 and beyond. The FY2028 step alone is 63.5% of PANW's entire FY2025 cost of subscription and support revenue. PANW cut what it owes in fiscal 2027 by 42% while adding 44% to the tail beyond fiscal 2031, and neither the filings nor the calls explain the reshaping.

9. The price moved on the multiple and not on the earnings estimate. Consensus twelve-month-forward EPS rose 2.5% between 2025-12-31 and 2026-08-28, from $4.06 to $4.16, while the price rose 101.7%; 96% of the calendar-2026 return, measured in logs, came from the forward multiple going from 45x to 89x, against 18% across the full decade. Forward FY2027 earnings estimates were cut 4.1% over the twelve months to 2026-07-31, and among the fourteen names in the cohort only Check Point shares that negative revision.

10. Every headline growth metric widens by acquisition, and the one that did not was retired. Total billings was guided every quarter from FY2020 to FY2024 and left the outlook on 2024-08-19, six months after the platformization guidance cut, having decelerated from 37.0% to 11.0% growth over two years and to roughly 3% in FY2025 on PANW's own formula. Billings was defined net of acquired deferred revenue; NGS ARR and remaining performance obligations, which replaced it, widen with each acquisition by PANW's own definition.

8. Management claim pressure tests

"Accretive to revenue growth and gross margin immediately post-close." Stated on slide 5 of the 2025-07-30 acquisition deck. In the first quarter with the assets, consolidated GAAP gross margin went from 72.9% to 67.6% and GAAP operating income from +$219m to −$183m. The claim holds only on the non-GAAP basis, where CyberArk's 84.8% cash gross margin exceeds PANW's, and the reconciling item is $117m a quarter of added purchased-intangible amortisation inside cost of subscription and support revenue. Both statements are the company's own; the deck did not say which basis it meant. Quantified: 5.3 points of GAAP gross margin and $402m of GAAP operating income in a single quarter.

"60% NGS ARR growth and 31% revenue growth show the platform working." PANW's own pro forma disclosure, combining both companies from the start of fiscal 2025, puts Q3 revenue at $3,043m against $2,621m, which is 16.1% growth, and nine-month pro forma at 17.4%. Organic NGS ARR grew 28% against 60% reported, and organic RPO 22% against 36%. The reported acceleration is consolidation arithmetic. Management gave the organic split at Q2 and Q3 FY2026 and said on 2026-06-02 that "our intention was always to make this a onetime in nature… Therefore, we'll be moving to total company guidance moving forward," so from FY2027 the organic rate stops being checkable.

"Our market share in hardware firewalls goes up 200 to 300 basis points every year." Arora, Q1 FY2025 call. Dell'Oro's last published split puts PANW at 29% of the firewall segment in 2Q 2024 against 28% in 3Q 2023, one point in two years. On the two most recent comparable quarters the movement runs the other way: Fortinet's product revenue grew 52% year over year to $773m in the June-2026 quarter against PANW's 31% to $594m in the April-2026 quarter, and the PANW figure includes CyberArk software licences. Both vendors take share from Check Point, whose product licences declined 14% in the same quarter.

"Palo Alto Networks remains the fastest-growing provider in the SASE market." The growth claim is supported: SASE ARR of $1.6bn growing 40% against a Dell'Oro SASE market growing 21% in 1Q 2026, with nearly 50 displacement wins worth about $200m of contract value in nine months.▪ The leadership claim is not. Gartner's 2026 SASE Platforms Magic Quadrant placed PANW third behind Netskope and Cato, down from first, citing constrained on-premises capability, with SDxCentral adding that "reportedly expensive pricing was one reason for its drop this year." The two statements measure different things, growth rate against execution and vision, and management has not addressed the change.

"XSIAM is best-in-class in what it does, and we've proven that." Q3 FY2026 call. Independent assessments do not show it. In Gartner's October 2025 SIEM Magic Quadrant, Splunk announced a Leader placement for the eleventh consecutive time and highest in Ability to Execute, and CrowdStrike's own release names its Visionary placement; PANW's blog describes "a strong debut" and names no quadrant (paloaltonetworks.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web]. Buyer reviews rate XSIAM expensive relative to Splunk and Microsoft Sentinel, and its SIEM-category mindshare on PeerSpot was 1.6% in August 2026, down from 2.9% a year earlier (peerspot.com, accessed 2026-08-29) [web]. PANW also left the MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise Evaluations in September 2025 after two rounds of 100% technique-level detection, so no current efficacy figure is independently measured.

"Growing nearly twice as fast as our closest next-generation SIEM competitor." Q3 FY2025 call, and true on the last comparable disclosure: at 2025-07-31 XSIAM ARR was roughly $410m growing about 170% against CrowdStrike's Falcon Next-Gen SIEM at above $430m growing 95% [web]. On level the two were within about $20m of each other, with CrowdStrike's book slightly the larger. Later module-level figures for CrowdStrike circulate from call commentary; its press releases give total ARR of $5.84bn at 2026-07-31 (+25%) and Falcon Flex ARR of $2.29bn (+101%) and no next-generation SIEM line, so the same-date comparison at $600m could not be verified against a primary source.

"The entire $20 billion TAM of SIEM." Q1 FY2025 call, later restated as a $40bn security-operations market. Third-party sizing puts SIEM at $8.39bn in 2026 growing to $13.67bn by 2031, and a bottom-up build from disclosed vendor revenue lands at $7-10bn. The $40bn figure holds only on a definition covering endpoint protection, managed detection and response, orchestration, attack-surface management and threat intelligence, most of which XSIAM does not address, and in which CrowdStrike's $5.84bn of ARR and Microsoft Defender are the incumbents.

"We are less than 5% penetrated into a TAM reaching nearly $300 billion." Q1 FY2026 call. Arithmetically correct against a denominator that has grown about 15x since 2018 while revenue grew about 5x. PANW's stated $59bn firewall-plus-SASE market for 2025 is 2.4-2.7x a Dell'Oro-based build of the same ground, and its $93bn security-operations-plus-cloud figure is more than 3x what SIEM and cloud-security vendor disclosure supports. In the one category with clean third-party vendor-share measurement, PANW holds roughly 29%.

"PAM controls extend from 8 million users to hundreds of millions." The acquisition deck pairs "8M CyberArk PAM Users Today" with ">1B Potential IAM Users" inside a $47bn 2028 identity market. Dividing the slides by each other gives $47 per user per year at the target against CyberArk's realised $158 of subscription ARR per user today, so blended realised price per identity has to decline about 70% for the volume expansion to fit inside the market management cites.▪ Arora said as much on the M&A call: "how do I work with my friend, Matt and Udi, to make sure that we can deliver privileged access to every user at a lower price. If I can unlock that, it doesn't matter what we paid."

"The strongest hardware performance in a decade." Q3 FY2026 call, with next-generation firewall bookings up nearly 40% year over year. Three disclosed things sit underneath it and management separated none of them: a new appliance generation entering volume, a 10% list price increase implemented in early April 2026 one month before the quarter closed, and an industry refresh Dell'Oro attributes to "AI infrastructure investment and risk-led refresh cycles." Arora also named the reversal: "you'll tell me before I can tell you when you see when data center growth starts to taper off or plateau, this thing is going to come to roost." Hardware is about 10% of revenue, so a 40% increase on a roughly $215m year-ago quarterly base adds about $85m, and the price rise caps how much of the 40% can be volume at about 30 points.▪

"We are 3 to 6 months ahead of our original time line for converging CyberArk's profitability with our own." Q3 FY2026 call, graded against an internal number that has not been published, so it cannot be checked. What is disclosed is the size of the gap and the cost booked against it: CyberArk ran an 18.1% non-GAAP operating margin in 2025 against PANW's guided 28.9-29.2%, and applying PANW's own FY2025 sales-and-marketing and general-and-administrative ratios to CyberArk's revenue base gives about $305m of annual cost to remove. The action booked so far is a workforce optimisation plan estimated at $59m in total, of which $41m was charged in Q3 FY2026 with $29m of that in sales and marketing, on a $21.1bn acquisition that added roughly 4,166 employees. One caution on the comparator: PANW's FY2025 general and administrative of 4.8% of revenue is a one-year low, depressed by a $135.3m contingent-consideration gain and a $38.8m litigation accrual release, against 8.5% in FY2024.

"Reducing our organic stock-based compensation expense as a percent of revenue by at least 300 basis points over the next 3 years." Q4 FY2023 call, with fiscal 2026 as the target year. On the disclosed GAAP basis it was missed: 15.6% of revenue in FY2023 against 16.8% across nine months of FY2026. Management's qualifier is "organic," which is not separately reported. Removing the $177m of CyberArk and Koi vesting acceleration and an estimated $95m-$150m of replacement-award amortisation, and removing acquired revenue, gives organic share-based compensation of 13.3-14.1% of organic revenue, a reduction of 150 to 230 basis points with one quarter left [estimate: nine-month FY2026 share-based compensation of $1,355m on $8,070m of revenue, adjusted for the disclosed acceleration and for replacement awards vesting over two to three years from each closing date].

The four inflections

February 2017, the go-to-market reset. Mark McLaughlin on the Q2 FY2017 call: "we overcomplicated our go-to-market motion with a lot more territory splits and segmentation than we've done in the past. This appears to have been too much too fast." Revenue growth went from 48.6% to 27.8% and never returned to the FY2016 rate. The cause was internal: the FY2017 territory splits were the same playbook the company had run for years, applied harder.

June 2018, Arora and the acquisition programme. A single-product company became a portfolio assembled by purchase. Product revenue went from 38.7% of the total to about 20%; employees from about 5,300 to 21,491. Arora named the target area on his first call: "We're also doing well in the nascent cloud security space. This is one area where I personally feel we could do a lot better." Eleven cloud and security-operations acquisitions followed over thirty months, and the build cost roughly two years of operating leverage — across FY2019-FY2021 revenue grew $1,357m while operating income declined $250m, an incremental margin of −18.4%.

February 2024, platformization. PANW approaches a customer before its point-product contracts expire, signs a multi-year consolidation commitment, and lets the customer start paying when the incumbent contracts end. Arora sized the giveaway at "about 6 months' worth of free product capabilities to our customers on a rolling basis." FY2024 landed 1.7% below the revenue guidance set in August 2023 and 6.7% below the original billings guidance, while operating margin came in above the original 25.0-25.5% guide. The cost restraint was headcount: employee growth went from 30.7% in FY2021 and 19.9% in FY2022 to 11.0%, 9.6% and 5.1% in FY2023-FY2025, and revenue per employee from $406k to $574k.

July 2025 to February 2026, CyberArk and Chronosphere. The prior twenty-five acquisitions averaged about $220m and bought technology PANW then scaled through its own channel. CyberArk cost $21,061m and bought an established competitor with about 10,000 customers and $1,440m of ARR. Arora acknowledged the break: "There's a fundamental difference in the way we've done acquisitions in the past. We believe that new vendors are going to come into place and replace existing legacy players. But in the identity space… this is not going to be a new vendor space." The guidance walk for one fiscal year measures what the two deals bought: revenue guidance +8.8%, NGS ARR +26.6%, non-GAAP EPS −1.8% at the midpoint, adjusted free cash flow margin −1.0 point, guided share count +7.2%.

How this company behaves

Under stress it names the cause and buys stock: the board added $500m to the repurchase authorisation on the afternoon of the 24% decline in February 2017; an accelerated repurchase was announced days before the COVID low in February 2020; $1,000m was repurchased at about $147.69 within weeks of the February 2026 trough. It answers a growth problem by reorganising how it sells — territory splits in FY2017, speedboat overlay teams in FY2020, deferred-payment platformization in FY2024 — and each produced a drawdown of 17% or more within two quarters. It sets multi-year targets on roughly a three-year cycle and replaces them: September 2019 set FY2022 targets, withdrawn in May 2020; September 2021 set FY2024 targets, met; February 2024 set FY2030 targets, raised in February 2026. And it has never written anything off. Asset impairment charges were $20.9m in FY2017, a leasehold at the former Santa Clara headquarters, and zero in every other year tagged from FY2015 through FY2025; no restructuring charge appears in any 10-K in the window; goodwill compounded from zero at 2013-07-31 to $21,902m with no impairment. The $59m CyberArk workforce optimisation plan initiated in fiscal Q3 2026 is its first named workforce action.
